title: More than a third of workers say they're hoarding expertise because they fear being replaced by the AI agents they're being asked to train
tldr: Over a third of workers admit to hiding their know-how because they fear training their own AI replacements, as companies capture keystrokes and workflows to automate jobs. A stark signal about trust, internal comms, and change management in the AI era.
why_fresh: new data on employee behavior shift
angle: Write about how AI-driven fear is quietly breaking knowledge-sharing culture — and what internal comms can do to rebuild trust.

title: The rise of the chief integrator: Communications' new power center
tldr: A new class of strategy/integration leaders is quietly becoming essential to making comms functions actually work, yet organizations under-invest in them. Reframes where power and value sit in modern comms teams.
angle: Profile the 'chief integrator' as the unsung operating backbone of communications teams.

title: The 2026 Global State of Internal Communications Report
tldr: New report argues the 'culture gap' has replaced engagement as the core internal-comms problem. Fresh framing and benchmark data for IC strategy.
angle: Unpack the 'culture gap' idea and what it means for how companies communicate internally.

title: How a content marketer became an award-winning cannabis creator
tldr: A content marketer turned creator breaks down how she scaled one of social's hardest-to-market categories. A concrete case study in human-led content and platform constraints.
angle: Use this as a template for building credibility in restricted or 'unmarketable' categories through personal, human content.

title: The Telegraph's next podcast play: video, events and paid memberships
tldr: The Telegraph is turning video podcasts into franchises spanning live events and paid memberships to deepen audience relationships. A concrete owned-media monetization and audience-loyalty playbook.
angle: Break down how publishers turn podcasts into multi-format audience ecosystems, not just shows.

title: How Domino's is taking on the Big Mac, Whopper and other fast-food icons
tldr: CMO Kate Trumbull explains the darkly comedic, hyperbolic tone behind Domino's latest campaign taking on fast-food icons. A useful CMO-level breakdown of tone-of-voice as strategy.
angle: Analyze how comedic risk-taking in brand voice signals confidence and cuts through category sameness.

title: 4 ways to get more from AI writing and editing, without losing your voice
tldr: A practical workflow for using AI as co-writer, editor and strategic partner while preserving your own voice. Directly useful for content ops and craft.
angle: Share your own AI-as-co-writer workflow and where the human voice must stay non-negotiable.

title: Smartphones Continue to Dominate Digital Media Usage
tldr: New data confirms smartphones keep dominating how people consume digital media. Useful baseline for media-consumption habits and format decisions.
angle: Tie mobile-first consumption data to why micro-content and vertical formats should lead content plans.

title: AI cannot optimize a company it cannot understand
tldr: Argues corporate AI can't optimize what it doesn't understand — putting a premium on clearly articulated goals, narrative and knowledge. Relevant to content governance and how orgs feed AI context.
angle: Argue that clear corporate narrative and content architecture are now prerequisites for useful AI.

title: Compliance-First Content Architecture
tldr: A five-component workflow for regulated finance brands to scale content without breaking governance. Concrete architecture for high-stakes content ops.
angle: Adapt compliance-first architecture principles for any brand that needs to scale trustworthy content.

title: In the age of AI, how much work you do matters less than it used to. Here's what matters more
tldr: With output nearly free thanks to AI, judgment and discretion become the most valuable skills. A useful reframe for creators competing on volume.
why_fresh: reframes value of work under AI
angle: Make the case that in an AI world, taste and judgment are the new content moat.

title: How the Meta Settlement Could Change the Internet
tldr: Deep look at how Meta's landmark settlement and teen-restriction terms could ripple across social platforms and the wider internet. Matters for anyone building audiences on social.
angle: Explore what tighter teen restrictions mean for brands' social reach and community strategy.

title: The Creator Economy Beyond YouTube and TikTok
tldr: Looks at where the creator economy is heading beyond the dominant platforms. Relevant for diversifying owned audience and platform risk.
angle: Map the emerging platforms and formats where creators are hedging against TikTok/YouTube dependence.

title: The Buffer Team Shipped 57 New Internal Tools in 5 Days
tldr: Buffer paused normal work so 72 people could build 57 internal tools in a week, including customer features. A concrete case study in low-code building and internal enablement culture.
angle: Explore 'build weeks' as a model for content and comms teams to ship their own tooling.
